items.q: Posterior blepharitis is distinguished from anterior disease chiefly by which findings?
o: Capped meibomian orifices, turbid expressed meibum and frothy tears
items.exp: Posterior disease is meibomian gland dysfunction with altered lipid layer causing evaporative dry eye; anterior disease crusts lashes (staphylococcal collarettes or seborrhoeic scales). Management targets glands with heat, massage and systemic tetracyclines.
r: Incorrect. Scales mark anterior seborrhoeic disease.
Correct. Meibomian capping and frothy tears.
Incorrect. Tear film destabilises in posterior disease.
items.kp: Frothy tears, capped oil holes: posterior blepharitis.

items.q: Painful acute swelling at the lid margin pointing outward with a lash at its apex is what and first treatment?
o: Hordeolum externum (stye); warm compresses, usually self draining
items.exp: Stye is an acute staphylococcal abscess of anterior glands; heat localises it and most rupture outward, antibiotics reserved for spreading cellulitis. Chalazion is chronic and painless.
r: Incorrect. Chalazion is painless and chronic.
Incorrect. Cancer grows slowly without acute pain.
Incorrect. Xanthelasma is painless lipid plaque.
items.kp: Hurts at the lash line: stye, heat it.

items.q: Firm painless tarsal nodule present 3 months with conjunctival granuloma on eversion most likely is what?
items.exp: Chalazion is sterile chronic granulomatous retention, managed conservatively then steroid injection or conjunctival incision and curettage; styes are acute and painful.
r: Incorrect. Cellulitis reddens and swells diffusely.
Incorrect. Tear sac sits medially below canthus.
items.kp: Painless months old lid lump: chalazion.

items.q: Recurrent chalazion-like lesion in a 70 year old with loss of lashes should prompt exclusion of what?
items.exp: Elderly meibomian malignancy mimics benign lumps, destroys lashes (madarosis), and needs full thickness biopsy with map sampling for pagetoid spread; repeated curettage without histology delays diagnosis.
r: Incorrect. Warts are papillomatous, not tarsal.
items.kp: Old lid lump that returns: rule out sebaceous cancer.

items.q: Involutional entropion is best corrected by addressing which mechanism?
o: Horizontal lid laxity with lower retractor disinsertion (tightening plus retractor repair)
items.exp: Ageing stretches canthal tendons and dehisces retractors, rotating the margin inward; lateral tarsal strip with retractor reinsertion restores tension. Skin excision alone recurs.
r: Incorrect. Levator lifts ptosis, not entropion.
Incorrect. Tarsorrhaphy narrows aperture for exposure.
items.kp: Lax lid rolling in: tighten and reattach.

items.q: Medial ectropion with watering in an elderly patient is explained and initially managed how?
o: Punctal eversion from lid laxity; lubricants then medial spindle or lid tightening surgery
items.exp: Lax lower lid everts the punctum from the tear lake, spilling tears (epiphora); surgery repositions punctum and tensions lid. Duct obstruction instead shows mucopurulent regurgitation on sac pressure.
items.kp: Lax lid spills tears: reposition the punctum.

items.q: Bell palsy with incomplete closure threatens the eye chiefly through what and needs which protection?
o: Exposure keratopathy; frequent lubricants, taping and moisture chamber
items.exp: Lagoons cornea dries and ulcerates, especially overnight; aggressive lubrication with lid taping bridges recovery, with gold weights or tarsorrhaphy for prolonged palsy.
r: Correct. Exposure needs taping and drops.
items.kp: Eye that cannot shut must be taped shut.

items.q: Commonest malignant eyelid tumour and its classic site and sign are what?
o: Basal cell carcinoma of lower lid with pearly rolled edge and telangiectasia
items.exp: Sun driven basal cell favours lower lid and medial canthus, ulcerating centrally (rodent ulcer) while sparing lashes early; excision with margin control cures most. Medial canthal lesions threaten lacrimal invasion.
r: Incorrect. Melanoma is rarer and pigmented.
items.kp: Pearly lower lid sore that never heals: basal cell.

items.q: Trichiasis threatens vision by which mechanism and definitive options?
o: Misdirected lashes abrading cornea causing ulcers; epilation stopgap with electrolysis, cryo or surgery
items.exp: Lash cornea touch (trachomatous, involutional or traumatic) erodes epithelium inviting bacterial ulcers and scarring; removing or redirecting follicles protects sight.
r: Correct. Lash abrasion needs follicle ablation.
items.kp: Lashes scraping cornea: ablate the follicles.

items.q: Ptosis with miosis, anhidrosis and apparent enophthalmos localises to which pathway?
items.exp: Oculosympathetic loss droops Muller muscle mildly, constricts pupil and dries ipsilateral face; third nerve ptosis is complete with down and out eye and dilated pupil.
items.kp: Droop plus tiny pupil plus dry cheek: Horner.
